prompt: Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins was commissioned to sculpt a series of life-size dinosaurs between 1852-54.  In this location, one species only had its head and back built with the rest of its body submerged underwater because they didn't know what it looked like then.  Where is this display located in 2024, which dinosaur species was this, and what did the rest of its body look like after all?
answer:
The display is still at the **Crystal Palace Dinosaur Court in Crystal Palace Park, south-east London**—the surviving outdoor dinosaur models commissioned by Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins in 1852–54.

The animal was **Labyrinthodon**, a name then used for a large Triassic “labyrinthodont” amphibian. It was not actually a dinosaur; the fossils known to Hawkins were chiefly skulls, so he modelled only its head and a little of its back, leaving the rest hidden beneath the lake’s surface.

Later discoveries showed that it was essentially a **large aquatic, salamander-like temnospondyl**, generally associated with **Mastodonsaurus**: a broad, flattened body, four short limbs and a substantial laterally flattened tail. Its exact soft-tissue form is still uncertain, but it was not the giant frog-like creature Hawkins imagined.
